result.decision_rationale:
The recorded Release build uses UMM 0.31.1.0, and three of the four pending findings are fixed. Ordinary packaging can still accept a stale DLL through two MSBuild import paths. The new selector check also rejects valid configuration.

Continuation for Claude

Keep the correction focused on build receipts. Check selectors in the already-imported LoaderReferences.targets, and account for an explicit project import before dropping a root targets file from the fingerprint. Refusing an import the receipt cannot track is sufficient. Narrow selector detection to property assignments so comments, ordinary values and item metadata remain usable.

Use the existing disposable checkout to demonstrate the two stale-receipt refusals and a successful build and package with harmless selector text. Retain the passing controls for genuinely shadowed files, unused siblings, empty import groups and active user hooks. Record the producing commit for each result and the required domain gate. The existing controller budget and the owner's IDE and native-testing scope apply.

executed_verification: The controller receipt records 416/416 domain tests passed at 8c6841a60e0580b62e10dc036e90ac48fedf96ff, exit 0, with an unchanged worktree.

The committed boundary report records 160 distinct passing cases on a clean temporary clone of 651295d. They include a genuine baseline package accepted by the standalone validator and the genuine UMM 0.33.0 release DLL rejected after lowering only its manifest. Git shows that only two evidence files changed between that run and the submitted commit.

The 8c198e0 build and package records and the 651295d suite agree on DLL SHA-256 634f22775c62bb34461fb202d85ab9d088f4e1cb1bd062e959812c8bcf9b12ee, MVID 7a6d0a75-f788-47a5-83c9-fed6fb14e3ff and ZIP SHA-256 b8cb456b8061fc48bfa464bd5af66f368516ab24cbb22d3d1f2c6e376d436e81. The recorded packaged references are UnityModManager 0.31.1.0 and 0Harmony12 1.2.0.1.

I verified the mission and amendment hashes and all 12 evidence-file digests listed in the index. Read-only PowerShell checks also confirmed the changed root-file filter and the selector matches on comments, values and XML metadata.
inspected: The fixed feature diff, the round-8-to-round-9 changes, AGENTS.md, both owner amendments, the prior ledger, the developer report and the controller evidence.
The manifest, pin verifier, production project import order, compiler inventory, receipt fingerprint, package and qualification callers, standalone ZIP validator and affected boundary fixtures.
The build and package records, API audit, loader profile inventory and newest-stable selection record.
limitations: The controller withheld the mixed foreground-session transcript. The domain result has a controller receipt. The other historical runs are supported by their committed structured outputs. This review used read-only checks.

The static audit records seven types and 25 members resolved on 0.31.1, 0.32.4, the owner's measured 0.33.0 and the selected 0.33.4. Native roll, assignment and persistence, mercenary and respec integration, and combined-stack execution are NOT RUN. The repository documents the lack of a disposable native harness.
The recorded build routes are the wrapper and command-line MSBuild. IDE execution remains unobserved under OWNER AMENDMENT 1.
required_gaps: Demonstrate refusal or correct receipt invalidation for a selector in LoaderReferences.targets and for an explicitly imported root targets file with a nearer conventional file present.
Demonstrate successful build and package admission with harmless selector text, alongside refusal of an actual selector assignment.
source_inspection_only: The stale-package outcomes in R8-F1 and R9-F1 follow from the import order, the fingerprint filter and the SkipCompilerExecution package evaluation. The read-only checks exercised the selection predicates. End-to-end results for those configurations are outstanding.

findings.actual: The new scan covers the conventional configuration files and the project file. It omits LoaderReferences.targets, which the project imports before Microsoft.CSharp.targets. The helper's own hash stays constant across reuse. The filter drops the selected sibling, and the package evaluation skips the production-only setting. Ordinary Package.ps1 can therefore accept the old receipt.
findings.blocking_rationale: A material change to the selected compiler configuration can leave a frozen DLL eligible for packaging.
findings.expected: A change to the selected file invalidates the receipt, or build and package admission both refuse the selector.
findings.requested_correction: Include the existing repository-owned LoaderReferences.targets in selector admission, or bind the file it selects. Preserve acceptance of an unused sibling.
findings.requested_evidence: In the disposable checkout, show refusal at both admission points or rejection of the old receipt after only the selected file changes. Show that restoring the original configuration permits packaging.
findings.title: The fingerprint can omit a targets file selected by tracked configuration
findings.trigger: Set DirectoryBuildTargetsPath in LoaderReferences.targets to a tracked src/Scratch/Directory.Build.targets. Build with that file empty, then change only that file to enable overflow checking during real compilation and package the existing DLL.

findings.actual: Line 299 exempts every project-file Import from the import check. Line 400 now drops the root file whenever the directory walk finds a nearer one. The previous candidate retained the root file. A production-only change in that explicit import is invisible to the package evaluation, and the project file's own bytes have stayed the same.
findings.blocking_rationale: The round-9 filter removes a previously fingerprinted input even when the production project explicitly uses it.
findings.expected: The receipt covers the explicitly imported root file, or admission refuses that import. A genuinely shadowed root file remains eligible for the existing reuse control.
findings.requested_correction: Account for explicit project imports when classifying a root targets file as shadowed, or refuse the conflicting import.
findings.requested_evidence: With both targets files present, show that the explicit-import case refuses stale reuse or refuses the configuration. Retain the passing case where the project has no explicit root import.
findings.title: A directly imported root targets file can disappear from the receipt
findings.trigger: Build with a tracked src/Directory.Build.targets and an explicit project import of the initially empty repository-root Directory.Build.targets. Change only the root file to set a production-only compiler option, then run ordinary Package.ps1.

findings.actual: The response-file check matches the selector word anywhere in the file. The XML check at line 295 inspects every element name. The predicates matched all three harmless inputs in a read-only check, so the wrapper throws before compilation and package admission throws before checking the receipt.
findings.blocking_rationale: This round introduces a build refusal for valid tracked configuration that leaves the import lookup untouched.
findings.expected: Comments, ordinary property values and item metadata are accepted. Assigning the import selector itself is refused.
findings.requested_correction: Recognize selector assignments in response-file switches and MSBuild property declarations. Ignore mentions that cannot set the property.
findings.requested_evidence: Show a successful build and matching package with a comment or unrelated property value in Directory.Build.rsp and inert XML metadata. Keep a real selector-assignment refusal as the negative control.
findings.title: Mentioning a selector in harmless configuration prevents a build
findings.trigger: Use a tracked Directory.Build.rsp containing the comment `# DirectoryBuildTargetsPath uses the default` or the option `/p:BuildNote=DirectoryBuildTargetsPath`. The XML equivalent is item metadata named DirectoryBuildTargetsPath.

findings.actual: The fixture prepends a forward-slash PATH entry, but Resolve-MSBuild gives an inherited MSBUILD_EXE_PATH precedence. The success detail prints the intended PATH entry regardless of which path the child used.
findings.blocking_rationale: The production normalization and the recorded Current-toolset controls support the prior fix. This affects the precision of the fixture on hosts with an executable override.
findings.expected: The case records the spelling returned by Resolve-MSBuild in the tested environment.
findings.requested_correction: Record the resolved child path in the existing case and check that it exercised the intended spelling.
findings.requested_evidence: If addressed, retain the separator spelling in the redacted path and record the selected toolset.
findings.title: The hook fixture can report a PATH lookup that the child did not use
findings.trigger: Run the suite with MSBUILD_EXE_PATH already pointing to the selected executable using backslashes.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The hook check normalizes the executable path, and the fingerprint applies the same conventional lookup at the root and below src. The 651295d record shows pre-rebuild receipt reuse with an inactive hook and with a genuinely shadowed root file. The active-hook and applicable-untracked-file refusal controls also pass.

The original Directory.Build.props trigger now fails at both build and package admission. The same DirectoryBuildTargetsPath selector in the project's existing LoaderReferences.targets still selects an untracked-by-the-receipt input. Changing only that selected file leaves the ordinary package check unsound.

The XPath now matches Import elements inside a group while allowing an empty group. The recorded empty-group build reproduced the original DLL and passed packaging. Adding the parent import to that group triggered refusal.

The fixture derives the active folder from the normalized executable path and chooses a distinct inactive version, including when 15.0 is selected. The measured run records Current as active and 15.0 as inactive.

summary.delivered_behavior: Dice Roller declares UMM 0.31.1, compiles against verified UnityModManager 0.31.1.0 and Harmony12 1.2.0.1, and inspects the packaged DLL before installation. The remaining defects concern build-receipt reuse and configuration admission.
remaining_owner_review: The owner retains the draft PR disposition and any decision to pursue disposable native qualification.
